CORE CLAIM SURVIVES VERBATIM; THE FAILURE SCENARIO DOES NOT. Severity corrected medium -> low.

WHAT I CONFIRMED MYSELF

1. C:/Users/samar/aarogya-grid/README.md:681 is exactly as quoted. The full command, with line numbers from `grep -n`, is:
   `gcloud run deploy aarogya-grid --source=. --region=asia-south1   --service-account=<sa>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com   --set-env-vars="GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<project>,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=asia-south1,GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true"`
   Four flags. No `--max-instances`, no `--min-instances`, no `--concurrency`, no `--timeout`.

2. README.md:684 heads the table `**What this project creates in a Google Cloud project, and what it costs.**` and README.md:690 is exactly as quoted: `| Cloud Run service, \`min-instances=1\`, \`max-instances=1\` | the only place workload identity can reach Vertex | ~Rs1,200-1,800/month, and the only recurring cost here |`. So three lines of table, nine lines below the command, inventory a service configuration that command does not create.

3. It really is the only user-facing deploy command. `grep -rn "gcloud run deploy"` returns two hits: README.md:681 and .claude/commands/verify.md:41. The second is a redeploy of the existing service and correctly leans on persistence — verify.md:43 says "Env vars and the service account persist across redeploys — do not re-pass them" — which is also true of scaling settings, so that one is not a defect.

4. Nothing sets it anywhere else: scoped grep over ts/tsx/mts/mjs/md/json/yaml/Dockerfile finds no `--max-instances`/`--min-instances`/`maxScale` flag outside prose. No service.yaml, no cloudbuild.yaml, no deploy npm script. Dockerfile sets only NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED/NODE_ENV/PORT/HOSTNAME.

5. No gate reads it. verify.mjs's only match for `instance|gcloud|describe|revision` is line 64, `e instanceof Error` — unrelated. scripts/check-claims.mts (1466 lines, and it does scan README.md: entries at :375, :380, :506 etc.) has zero hits for max-instances/min-instances/gcloud.

6. The invariant is asserted more widely than the reporter said: besides the six code sites, `min-instances=1` is also load-bearing at src/lib/durable/sink.ts:660 and src/lib/overlay/runtime-forecast.ts:21, and the cap is owned as a judge-facing limit at DEFENSE.md:161, DEFENSE.md:194 and SUBMISSION.md:84.

7. The "it was 4 until 12 Sep" detail checks out — `git log -S max-instances` surfaces commit d1c424a, "Make the one-instance claim true, and cap the cache that assumes it": "README.md, api/events/route.ts and overlay/store.ts all state that the service runs `--max-instances=1` ... The service was at `maxScale=4`. So the feature shipped this session was ... documented as safe on a precondition that did not hold, in three places. Now `maxScale=1` (revision 00017)."

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE REPRODUCTION LENS

a) "Two browser tabs now land on different containers" does not reproduce, and this is the finding's whole demonstrated harm. Cloud Run's default request concurrency is 80 per instance; two SSE streams are two concurrent requests. Cloud Run does not start a second container until concurrency saturates. A reviewer with two tabs gets one instance even at max-instances=100 — which is precisely the rehearsal d1c424a itself ran ("two tabs in 282 ms"). You need roughly 80+ simultaneous held connections before instance two exists, which no reviewer generates by hand.

b) "The global rate limit of 240/600 s becomes 24,000" needs all 100 instances live, i.e. ~8,000 concurrent requests. Worse for the reporter, src/lib/rate-limit.ts:244-246 deliberately does not say "=1" — it says the deployment "pins `--max-instances` precisely so that multiplier is a known, small integer rather than an autoscaling surprise". That sentence is not falsified by a cap of 4, and is the one cited comment the fresh-deploy case actually breaks only in the weakest sense.

c) The hydrate claim misreads the code. store.ts:228-245's docstring scopes the renumber path to a single trigger: "The one case that can break that is a restore which FAILED: the instance starts counting from 1 again and writes rows whose seq collides with older ones." It is not written about, and does not describe, two concurrent instances. The reporter's "hydrate on each instance renumbers independently" is inference presented as code reading.

d) The drift half is a known, already-actioned concern rather than an unnoticed one: the project caught the identical mismatch, fixed the live service to maxScale=1, and recorded the revert command in d1c424a's message.

WHY LOW AND NOT NONE, AND NOT MEDIUM

Not none: the divergence itself does reproduce with concrete inputs — fresh project plus README.md:681 yields a service whose `autoscaling.knative.dev/maxScale` is unset, i.e. 100, and `minScale` 0, so the README's own resource inventory nine lines down is wrong about the service its own command builds, and the ~Rs1,200-1,800/month figure is derived from a min-instances=1 the command never sets. That is not style, and it is not re-litigating the one-instance decision — it is the copy-paste command diverging from a decision the project documents in eight places and once committed a fix for. Pointedly, d1c424a fixed the running service but left the instructions that reproduce the wrong configuration untouched.

Not medium: no shipped number moves. Nothing on /, /console or the deck changes; check-claims' figure discipline is untouched. The judged artefact is the live URL, which is known-correct at maxScale=1 and whose setting survives the redeploy path verify.md documents. The blast radius is a third party doing a fresh self-deploy and then load-testing it — and the one harm a hackathon reviewer would plausibly try, two tabs, provably does not fire. Reporter confidence "certain" is not warranted for the consequences, only for the two README lines.

findings.title: 12 published surge signals carry observedValue 0 against expectedUpperBound 0 under a "Rising consumption" label
findings.evidence:
Signal as shipped and as served live at /api/indicators:

  {"id":"sig-945507ab","hazardClass":"vector_borne",
   "hazardLabel":"Rising consumption of Anti-Snake Venom (polyvalent) (monsoon envenomation)",
   "area":{"code":"DST-36-MAHABUBN","name":"Mahabubnagar",...},
   "observedFrom":"2026-09-22","observedTo":"2026-09-23",
   "metric":"medicine_consumption_units",
   "observedValue":0,"expectedUpperBound":0,"exceedanceRatio":0,"confidence":"low"}

12 of the 297 signals are of this shape (all ASV-POLY-10ML: Mahabubnagar, Barpeta x2, Nagaon x2, Dibrugarh x3, Lucknow, Rewa, Hyderabad, Kurnool). The live feed is byte-identical to the repo artefact apart from an added "schema" pointer.

Root cause, two lines:

  scripts/detect-anomalies.mts:193   v: Math.round(a.values[i]),
  scripts/detect-anomalies.mts:195   hi: +a.upper[i].toFixed(1),

sub-unit series cache as v:0, hi:0 — the backing row in src/data/anomalies.json is
  {"d":"2026-09-22","v":0,"lo":0,"hi":0,"p":0.356,"dir":"high"}

then the excess gate loses its teeth:

  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:86   .filter((p) => p.dir === 'high' && p.v >= p.hi * (1 + rule.excessAboveUpperBound))

with hi === 0 this is `0 >= 0`, true for every point regardless of value. Re-running the rule over src/data/anomalies.json reproduces all 297 published warnings, of which 21 fire on runs whose summed upper bound is 0.
findings.failureScenario: A judge follows the README's "297 signals leave the building at /api/indicators ... the BRICS early-warning hook, built as a contract", opens the live feed, and finds an outbreak signal that says a district's Anti-Snake Venom consumption is rising while the same record states that zero units were consumed over the two-day window and zero were expected. The row contradicts itself, and 7% of the feed fires from a threshold test that is arithmetically incapable of rejecting anything.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the detector's sub-unit precision instead of rounding at scripts/detect-anomalies.mts:193-195 (e.g. +a.values[i].toFixed(2) and +a.upper[i].toFixed(2)), and make the gate at src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:86 non-vacuous — require p.v > p.hi as well as p.v >= p.hi * (1 + e), or floor the comparison band at a minimum unit. Re-running scripts/tune-warning.mts afterwards will move the published detection/false-alarm/precision figures, so those need re-deriving in the same pass.

findings.title: exceedanceRatio is not observedValue / expectedUpperBound for 21 of 297 signals in the interop feed
findings.evidence:
The contract, stated in the Warning interface:

  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:64   /** `observed / expectedUpperBound`. How far above normal, as a multiple. */
  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:65   ratio: number;

The implementation floors the denominator:

  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:101   expectedUpperBound: +run.reduce((a, p) => a + p.hi, 0).toFixed(1),
  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:102   ratio: +(
  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:103     run.reduce((a, p) => a + p.v, 0) / Math.max(1, run.reduce((a, p) => a + p.hi, 0))
  src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:104   ).toFixed(3),

Measured over the shipped feed: 33 of 297 signals have expectedUpperBound < 1, and for 21 of them the published ratio demonstrably differs from observedValue/expectedUpperBound. Worst cases:

  sig-aa13ac1b  observed 5  expectedUpperBound 0.2  published 5  actual 25
  sig-d903da02  observed 3  expectedUpperBound 0.2  published 3  actual 15
  sig-c9ab73c0  observed 3  expectedUpperBound 0.2  published 3  actual 15
  sig-59f8c2a1  observed 4  expectedUpperBound 0.4  published 4  actual 10

and 9 more where expectedUpperBound is 0 and the published ratio is simply the observed count.

The published schema documents no floor:
  docs/indicator-schema.json — properties.signals.items.properties.exceedanceRatio = {"type":"number","minimum":0}

exceedanceRatio also feeds confidenceFor() at scripts/export-indicators.mts:145, so the published confidence tier inherits the floored value.
findings.failureScenario: A downstream consumer of the advertised country-agnostic feed (or a judge spot-checking it) recomputes observedValue / expectedUpperBound to rank signals and gets 25x where the payload says 5x. The feed's own schema gives no way to know the denominator was floored at 1, so the two numbers cannot be reconciled from the payload alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Either publish the ratio the field claims and handle the small-denominator case by omitting exceedanceRatio (or emitting null) when expectedUpperBound rounds below one unit, or keep the floor and say so — rename the field, document the floor in docs/indicator-schema.json as a description, and correct the docstring at src/lib/surge/warnings.ts:64 so the implementation and the contract agree.

findings.title: The pitch deck says 37.21 Cr people in catchment; the live site says 37.22 Cr from the same snapshot total

docs/pitch-deck.html:367
37.21 Cr
people in catchment
The artefact: src/data/national-snapshot.json totals.populationCovered = 372164015 (verified: exactly the sum of all 128 district rows and of src/data/census-2011.json). findings.title: forecast-cache.json ships 54 inverted 90% prediction intervals (lower bound above upper bound)
findings.evidence:
Series DST-36-KHAMMAM|ASV-POLY-10ML, first four horizon days as shipped:
  m  : [0.09, 0.11, 0.01, 0]
  lo : [0.09, 0.09, 0.02, 0]
  hi : [0,    0,    0,    0]

Day index 1 has lo 0.09, m 0.11, hi 0 — the 90% band's upper bound sits below both the mean and the lower bound. Series DST-09-LUCKNOW|ASV-POLY-10ML day 6: lo 0.16, m 0.04, hi 0.1.

Swept across all 6,016 x 21 = 126,336 points: 54 with lo > hi, 59 with m > hi, 644 with lo > m, touching 219 of 6,016 series. No NaN, no Infinity, no negatives, and lengths are uniformly 21.

The consumer clamps the symptom rather than the cause:
  src/lib/forecast/timesfm.ts:160
    return f.mean.map((_, d) => Math.max(0, (f.upper[d] - f.lower[d]) / (2 * z)));

so an inverted band silently yields a zero implied sigma instead of an error. The cache is a faithful 2-dp record of what AI.FORECAST returned (scripts/forecast-refresh.mts:160-165 only rounds), so this is a model quantile-crossing artefact that is being shipped unflagged rather than a computation error here.
findings.failureScenario: A judge downloads the 2.5 MB forecast cache the README points at and plots the band for any of the 219 affected series — most of them anti-snake-venom and antidote lines whose demand is near zero — and the shaded 90% interval renders inside-out, with the upper edge beneath the forecast line. Nothing in the file says the model's quantiles crossed.
findings.suggestedFix: Either normalise on write in scripts/forecast-refresh.mts (sort each day's lo/m/hi triple, or set lo = min(lo, m) and hi = max(hi, m)) and record in the cache header that crossing quantiles were repaired, or count the crossings into the cache metadata alongside seriesDeclined/seriesMissing so the artefact discloses them. Replacing the Math.max(0, ...) clamp at src/lib/forecast/timesfm.ts:160 with an explicit check would stop a crossed band reading as zero uncertainty.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — the finding survives independent verification, and is stronger than reported. VERBATIM CHECK (all three cited lines say what the reporter claims): - SUBMISSION.md:19, inside the `> Description` block opened at :16 that is pasted into the submission form: "> **TimesFM** forecasts demand for every facility–drug pair, an anomaly detector flags outbreak" - README.md:4 (first paragraph): "demand for every facility–drug pair, spots outbreak surges days before a shelf empties, and moves" - docs/pitch-deck.html:334, in the title slide's

: "TimesFM forecasts demand for every facility–drug pair, the detector spots an" REPRODUCTION — the claim is false against the code path, not merely loose: src/lib/forecast/timesfm.ts:68-80 documents the gate and refutes the lede itself: "A class goes to TimesFM only where it beat Croston by a margin worth a dependency on a hosted model; everything else stays on the incumbent." and "Keyed by the FACILITY series' pattern, which the pipeline already has as fit.pattern". The gate is applied per facility series, and src/data/national-snapshot.json forecast.byPattern routes only `intermittent` to timesfm; smooth, erratic and lumpy all go to croston. scripts/build-snapshot.mts:480-481 counts the outcome per position (`if (st.forecastSource === 'timesfm') timesfmPositions++; else crostonPositions++;`), giving timesfmPositions 30,535 + crostonPositions 50,569 = 81,104 = totals.trackedPositions. So 50,569 facility–drug pairs (62.4%) never touch a TimesFM path. I tried and could not construct any reading under which TimesFM serves "every facility–drug pair"; the strongest available defense (that TimesFM is invoked on all 6,016 district×drug series and the gate only picks where its output is used) fails because the gate is keyed at facility level and the shipped per-position count is what the artefact publishes. THE PROJECT'S OWN CODE MAKES THIS THE CARDINAL SIN: src/lib/snapshot-types.ts:254-261 — "Counted rather than asserted. 'Forecasting runs on Google's TimesFM' is the central AI claim of this submission, and a claim like that should be answerable from the artefact." timesfm.ts:61-64 — "a judge asking 'is this row actually TimesFM?' deserves an answer from the artefact rather than from a README." The README is exactly where the wrong answer lives. SELF-CONTRADICTION CONFIRMED: README.md:71 "It does not serve every position, and that is a measurement rather than a compromise." and :75-76 "It won **intermittent** demand by 6.5% and holds **30,535** of the **81,104** shipped positions". docs/pitch-deck.html:495 "It wins intermittent demand by 6.5% and holds 30,535 of 81,104 shipped positions." THE GUARD GENUINELY CANNOT CATCH IT: scripts/check-claims.mts:345-353 defines the claim union; :1406-1407 evaluates `must` as a bare `text.includes(c.must)`, a presence check blind to a contradicting sentence elsewhere in the same file. The `mustNot` mechanism exists and is used at :950, :955, :962, :971, :1012 and :1015, but none covers this phrase; grep over the whole repo for "every facility" returns no guard rule, only the three surfaces plus unrelated code comments. Both sentences therefore coexist in README.md and the gate passes. PROVENANCE CONFIRMED: `git log -S "forecasts demand for every facility"` -> 411239e; `git show 411239e` adds in the same commit both "+TimesFM forecasts demand for every facility–drug pair" and "+... holds 30,535 of 81,104 shipped positions". The fix landed in the body, the stale framing was written fresh into the lede. STRONGER THAN REPORTED: `grep -n "30,535\|81,104\|Croston\|intermittent" SUBMISSION.md` returns NOTHING. Unlike README and the deck, SUBMISSION.md carries no corrective figure anywhere, so the pasted form Description travels alone and uncorrected. Its guard rules (check-claims.mts:410-447) pin reach, seriesForecast ("over 6,016 series"), the federated numbers and the assistant latency, but nothing ties the universality claim to timesfmPositions. NOT VERIFIED (does not change the verdict): docs/pitch-deck.pdf has no extractable text layer (843k glyph bytes recovered, "timesfm" absent as text), so I could not confirm whether the compiled PDF carries the phrase. The three cited surfaces are confirmed in source. SEVERITY: critical. The brief's rubric names "a claim that is false" as critical, and this is the single most consequential AI claim in the submission, on the text pasted into the form, with no guard covering it and no correction in that file. The user's own memory index independently flags "TimesFM scores every position" as stale.

REFUTED. The mechanical half of the finding is real; every load-bearing claim built on top of it is false.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
- `src/lib/optimize/redistribute.ts:42-45` does read `HARD CONSTRAINTS / 1. A donor may never fall below its own reorder point.`
- Pass 2's quantity is genuinely not bounded by the reorder point: `rescueRoom = donor.risk.onHand - (state.given.get(capKey(donor)) ?? 0) - mustRetainUnits(donor)` (line 1005-1006) and `grep -n 'reorderPoint' src/lib/optimize/redistribute.ts` returns only lines 220, 303, 745, 1279 — none inside pass 2.
- `grep -n 'reorderPoint' scripts/verify-guardrails.mts` returns nothing.
- 55 of 5,578 shipped orders match the pass-2 signature (riskReduction === 0 && wasteAvertedUnits >= quantity).

WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED

1. The failure scenario does not reproduce — it stops three lines short of the code. The reporter computes `rescuable = min(40, 120, 48) = 40` and declares "the planner can ship 40 units." Execution does not end there. Lines 1086-1093 run per order:
   `if (donor.risk.onHand - rescueGiven - qty < mustRetainUnits(donor)) continue;`
   `const rescueAfter = stockoutProbabilityAt(rescueSamples, donor.risk.onHand - rescueGiven - qty);`
   `if (!donorIsSafe(rescueAfter, rescueBefore)) continue;`
   With the reporter's own numbers this rejects the candidate. `reorderPoint = Math.ceil(quantile(sorted, serviceLevel))` with `serviceLevel = 0.95` (src/lib/forecast/risk.ts:387, 447), so rp = 100 means the 95th percentile of lead-time demand is 100. `donorIsSafe` (line 614-619) requires `after <= 0.10 - 0.005` AND `after <= before + 0.02 - 0.005`, where before = P(demand > 120) <= 0.05. Leaving the donor at 80 therefore requires P(80 < demand <= 120) <= 0.015 while F(100) = 0.95 — i.e. 1.5% of the mass in a window that straddles the 95th percentile. The candidate hits `continue` and no order ships. The reporter names this guardrail in the evidence and then builds a scenario the guardrail kills.

2. The empirical claim "55 such orders ship" is falsified by the shipped artefact. All 55 pass-2 orders carry `donorStockoutAfter === 0` — zero of 2,000 lead-time samples exceed what the order leaves the donor, so remaining stock >= max(samples) >= p95 = the reorder point. Across all 5,578 orders in src/data/districts the maximum `donorStockoutAfter` is 0.0415, below the 0.05 that corresponds to sitting exactly at the reorder point; docs/guardrail-gate.json independently reports `worstDonorStockoutAfter: 0.0305` over 196 audited donors. Not one shipped order, pass-2 or otherwise, leaves a donor below its reorder point. (Direct onHand/reorderPoint arithmetic is unavailable: district `positions` arrays are filtered to severity critical|high — `[...new Set(d.positions.map(p=>p.severity))]` → ['critical','high'] — and all 47 distinct donor facility|drug pairs in the national plan are absent from them. donorStockoutAfter is the available evidence and it points one way.)

3. The reporter truncated the comment they quoted as "says the opposite." The full comment at lines 995-1005 names the bound that replaces the reorder point and cites the bug that motivated it ("a CHC gave away 436 pairs of sterile gloves against a 228-unit fraction cap and was left 136 against a 190-unit cover floor"). The carve-out is documented a second time at lines 594-601 on `PlannerState.given`: "the expiry-rescue pass may move stock a facility holds BELOW its reorder point -- units it was going to lose anyway -- so capacity and cumulative giving are genuinely different quantities, and the guardrail binds on the second." Twice-documented with rationale is a deliberate decision, not drift.

4. The category is wrong: nothing published carries the reorder-point wording. The claim on the landing page is "we never create a stock-out to fix one" (redistribute.ts:817, verify-guardrails.mts:7, types.ts:282), and DEFENSE.md:113-127 states it as exactly three numeric limits — 40% of shelf, 21/14/7 days cover, P(out) <= 10% and <= +2pp. No surface claims the reorder-point version, so no surface disagrees with its artefact.

5. "Nothing re-derives constraint 1" is wrong about the constraint that is actually published. verify-guardrails.mts:163-172 sums `t.quantity` over `plan.transfers` per (donor, drug) — every order, every pass, pass 2 included — then re-derives all three caps at lines 204-230 from an independent 2,000-sample redraw. CORE DEFECT: CONFIRMED. Every cited line says what the reporter claims, and I verified the chain independently.

- `redistribute.ts:289-293` — `mustRetainUnits` returns `Math.max(onHand*(1-maxDonorFraction), coverFloorDays*demand)`, a FLOAT, with no floor.
- `redistribute.ts:1008-1010` — `rescueRoom = onHand - given - mustRetainUnits(donor)`; `rescuable = Math.min(wasteBudget, onHand, rescueRoom)` inherits the float.
- `redistribute.ts:1062-1068` — that float goes in as `cap` to `allocateFefo(donor, Math.min(rescuable, absorbable), 3, ...)`.
- `redistribute.ts:356-360` — only the BATCH is floored (`Math.floor(batch.quantity)`); `take = Math.min(free, cap - quantity)` lets the fractional cap bind, contradicting the function's own comment at 354-355 ("a pick list cannot ask for a fraction of a dispensing unit").
- `redistribute.ts:1069` — `if (qty < 1) continue` does not reject fractions.
- The pass-1/pass-2 asymmetry is real: `donatableUnits` (line 304) wraps in `Math.floor`; the rescue path does not.
- Shipped: 19 of 5,578 orders in `src/data/districts/` carry non-integer `quantity`, all pass-2 rescues (riskReduction 0).

BUT TWO LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS ARE FALSE, and both inflate the severity.

1. The flagship example does not reproduce. `DST-09-GORAKHPU-CHC-001|DST-09-GORAKHPU-CHC-003|ARV-VACCINE` is a DUPLICATE id in that file — index 20 has quantity 21, index 58 has 25.799999999999997. `service.ts:262` uses `detail.orders.find(o => o.id === input.orderId)`, which returns the FIRST. 2. The default click fails, and re-typing the rounded-up display fails, but a one-keystroke correction works. Recoverable, not blocked.

CONSEQUENCE (the lens): small.
- 18/5,578 orders = 0.32%, in 13 of 128 districts.
- All are pass-2 rescues with riskReduction 0, appended at the TAIL of each district's list (idx 56/66, 119/125, 112/116, 73/74, 61/70...). A judge would have to scroll to the bottom of one of 13 specific districts and click Dispatch on one of the least-interesting cards.

- Published aggregates are untouched: total fractional excess across the whole country is exactly 10.000 units. ₹2.48 Cr, 7,097 orders and 4,683 critical do not move in any displayed digit, so this is NOT the "number that disagrees with its artefact" class the brief flags as most serious.
- The reporter's "falsifies HARD CONSTRAINT 4" is a stretch on the literal text (constraint 4 is about batch-holding and double-promising, both still satisfied), though the closing sentence "a quantity a storekeeper cannot pick is not a recommendation" is fairly invoked.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING: the shipped plan contains physically meaningless quantities (25.799999999999997 vials, 3772.8 tablets); the raw float is visible in live page source; `csv.ts:158 cell(line.quantity)` writes it into the exported indent, in a file whose own docstring (csv.ts:88-92) says fractional units "disagree with the physical shelves"; and no guard covers it — `verify-batch-bounds.mts` is marked "THROWAWAY ... Delete after running" and only checks `l.quantity > Math.floor(held)`, which a fractional 531.2 against a larger batch passes. One-line fix: floor `rescuable` at line 1010, matching `donatableUnits`.

Medium, not high: a real bug on a reachable live path, but 0.32% reach at the tail of the list, an easy user workaround, zero effect on any published figure, and the stated blocking scenario is false.

I reproduced it rather than reasoning about it: a scratchpad script importing the repo's real FixedWindowLimiter/GLOBAL_RULE/PER_CLIENT_RULE and replaying proxy.ts:176-184 gave `240 POST /api/ask from one IP -> 20 served, 220 rejected as client`, global remaining 0, then `POST /api/commit -> 429 scope global`, `POST /api/dispatch -> 429 scope global`, still blocked at T0+599s, clear at T0+600s; and the organic path `12 clients x 20 asks = 240 offered; 13th client commit allowed? false`. But two premises of the finding are false, and they are what carried the severity. (1) "a budget that exists solely to cap the model bill, which those endpoints never spend" is contradicted by the code's own docs: proxy.ts:56-62 gives /api/commit an independent reason to be metered ("re-simulates every carrier... several hundred inventory simulations... a denial of service in a loop"), and proxy.ts:28-29 and :86-89 designate the global counter as the only non-forgeable ceiling ("Forgery is answered by the global counter, not by this key"). Exempting commit/dispatch from the shared bucket, which is what the finding asks for, would leave commit's CPU vector bounded only by a client-supplied x-forwarded-for - strictly worse. (2) The attacker gains no new capability: 240 POSTs aimed at /api/commit itself fill the same bucket and produce the identical denial, and at max-instances=1 the single container is the softer target regardless. Category "security" therefore overstates it; this is availability coupling, self-healing within one 600s fixed window, answered with an explanatory 429 body, with no data loss, no unauthorized access, and no published number affected.

What genuinely survives is minor and citable: rate-limit.ts:212-216 describes the bucket as "240 model-backed POSTs" while it in fact gates two paths that are not model-backed; and proxy.ts:119-121 tells the caller "the consoles, forecasts and dispatch plans are unaffected" in the very response that refuses a /api/dispatch action. Organic tripping needs 240 metered POSTs inside one 10-minute window with no client-side retry loops anywhere (GridAssistant.tsx:256, CaptureConsole.tsx:508, DispatchTicketStrip.tsx:90 each fire one fetch per user action), i.e. ~12 concurrent judges at their full 20-request budget. Real, reproducible, but minor: low, not medium.

A judge reloading during the cold start aborts /api/overlay, which owns no timers. The headline reproduction is refuted.

The window survives only on paths that bypass the overlay seed while the restore is still unsettled: (a) an already-open console whose EventSource auto-reconnects (retry: 5000, route.ts:108) straight to /api/events after a redeploy replaces the container — that reconnect is then the first caller of ensureRestored; (b) a second client hitting /api/events while another tab's /api/overlay is still driving the restore; (c) a cold-start-free variant where signalFromNodeResponse returns `AbortSignal.abort(...)` because `res.errored || res.destroyed` at construction, so GET starts with an already-aborted signal. All three need a disconnect inside a one-per-container ~1-2 s window (or a very tight queueing race for (c)). The common case is clean: on a warm container a tab close fires res 'close' long after line 185 registered, so shutdown runs. Live probe confirms the warm steady state: /api/events time_starttransfer=0.162s, /api/overlay time_total=0.212s.

THE REPORTER UNDER-COUNTED, NOT OVER-COUNTED

districts[].resources has 29 keys; NationalConsole reads 12 (lines 331-349). That leaves 17 unused, not 11. I could not reproduce the 8,245 B gzipped figure exactly (an isolated blob of the same fields gzips to 6,947 B at level 6). Marginal gzip cost of a subset inside a larger stream is not a well-defined standalone number. This does not affect the finding, which already frames the saving as small.

This is a real, measured, verified inefficiency with a concrete fix (project the snapshot server-side before passing it), and it is not a re-litigation of a documented decision — the page.tsx docstring justifies reading a precomputed snapshot, but never addresses shipping every field to the client. QUOTES CONFIRMED, CONCLUSION REFUTED. The text exists exactly as reported — docs/forecast-runtime.md:38 reads "**A full refresh of all 6,016 series is 4 batches, ≈ 224–295 s run back to back** at the measured rate, against a 180 s budget. Sequential batching misses it at both ends; the refresh has to run its batches concurrently." DEFENSE.md:154 and :166 are also verbatim ("All **6,016** … in **three BigQuery statements**" … "→ `docs/forecast-runtime.md` · README, *Scaling across India*"), as are scripts/forecast-refresh.mts:54 (`const MAX_QUERIES = 3;`), :106 (`const perBatch = Math.ceil(wire.length / MAX_QUERIES);`) and :122 (the refusal). So the reporter did not misquote anything. But the finding does not survive as a defect, for four independent reasons.

(1) BOTH NUMBERS ARE TRUE, AND OF DIFFERENT BATCH SIZES. I read the generator at scripts/forecast-ladder.mts:382-383 and the artefact it consumes. docs/forecast-runtime.json has seriesPool 6016 and a top passing rung of requestedSeries 2000, so `Math.ceil(o.seriesPool / top.requestedSeries)` = ceil(6016/2000) = 4. Four batches of ≤2,000 is 3 full plus a 16-series runt — arithmetically correct. Production packs 2,006 (ceil(6016/3), confirmed against src/data/demand-district-daily.json: 6,016 series) and gets 3. Neither is wrong; they are different batch sizes, and docs/forecast-runtime.md:30 says so explicitly in the same bullet list — "the batch size is set by design rather than forced by the ceiling."

(2) THE SENTENCE'S OWN TIMING NUMBER PROVES IT IS NOT DESCRIBING THE PRODUCTION PATH AS FOUR STATEMENTS, AND IS INTERNALLY CONSISTENT. From forecast-runtime.json, the 2,000 rung is wallClockMinMs 74324 / wallClockMaxMs 98157. The generator extrapolates per series: (74324/2000)*6016/1000 = 223.5 → 224 s; (98157/2000)*6016/1000 = 295.2 → 295 s. That is the time for 6,016 series of work — exactly what "3 full batches + a 16-series runt" costs. The band is not 4×74.3–4×98.2 (297–393 s). The figure is honest and self-consistent.

(3) THE "4 BATCHES" LINE IS THE DOCUMENTED ANTECEDENT OF THE SHIPPED DESIGN, NOT DRIFT FROM IT. scripts/forecast-refresh.mts:21-24 cites this very figure as its reason: "Three, not four. 6,016 series at the ladder's round 2,000 is four batches and fails the gate by one. The batch size is therefore derived -- ceil(seriesCount / MAX_QUERIES) -- which gives 2,006 series and a 595 KB statement, comfortably inside the 1,024 K limit. Measured, not assumed." The doc's other conclusion — "the refresh has to run its batches concurrently" — is likewise implemented at forecast-refresh.mts:131 (`await Promise.all(...)`), and its 180 s budget is the same one asserted at :214. The doc argues *for* the shipped design; it does not contradict it. Reporting it is re-litigating a trade-off the codebase documents at length, which the audit rules exclude.

(4) THE DOC IS MACHINE-GENERATED AND COULD NOT SAY "3" WITHOUT LYING. Lines 3-4 and the renderMarkdown docstring (forecast-ladder.mts:373-379) state nothing is typed by hand. The ladder measured rungs of 200/500/1000/2000; it never measured 2,006. Rewriting the bullet to "3 batches" would put a number in a "measured, not estimated" table that the run did not measure — strictly worse than the status quo.

WHAT SURVIVED MY CHECK

1. The line says what the reporter quotes. src/lib/district-detail.ts:397-408, verbatim: line 398 "Every critical and high position in the district."; lines 404-405 "Within one district all ~630 positions are present, so the tier filter has real rows behind every chip." The emitter at :561-562 is exactly `states.filter((s) => s.risk.severity === 'critical' || s.risk.severity === 'high')`.

2. Every measured figure reproduces exactly. Over all 128 files in src/data/districts/: positions min 12, median 62, mean 80.3, max 231. trackedPositions mean 633.6, sum 81,104 (= the "~630"). ZERO of 128 payloads carry trackedPositions-many rows. Lucknow: 203 in file vs trackedPositions 915, with criticalPositions 94 + highPositions 109 = 203. Only `critical` (4,683) and `high` (5,591) appear as severities anywhere in the 128 payloads. So the sentence at :405, read as a description of the `positions: PositionRow[]` field it annotates, is false for every shipped payload, and it contradicts line 398 seven lines above it.

WHY IT IS LOW, NOT MEDIUM

The brief defines medium as "a latent bug or a real inefficiency". There is no latent bug here, and the reporter's failure scenario is defused three ways:

(a) The consequence a misled reader would draw is TRUE anyway, and enforced in code, not by payload completeness. src/components/DistrictConsole.tsx:564: `TIERS.filter((t) => (tierCounts[t.key] ?? 0) > 0).map(...)` — a tier with zero rows is never rendered as a chip at all. The reporter's scenario ("a tier whose facilities are all healthy contributes zero rows") is true at the payload level but produces no visible defect: the chip is simply not drawn. So "real rows behind every chip" holds.

(b) Nothing propagates. Every consumer of the array labels it correctly: DistrictConsole.tsx:555 renders "{visiblePositions.length} of {detail.positions.length} critical + high"; src/lib/ai/grid-tools.ts:789 names it `criticalAndHighPositions: detail.positions.length`. The district page header (DistrictConsole.tsx:251) and methodology note (:1027) both use `d.trackedPositions` (915 for Lucknow), not the array length. No published number is wrong because of this sentence, and scripts/check-claims.mts:62 only reads `payload.positions` for leadTimeDays — it asserts no completeness.

(c) The docstring self-corrects: its FIRST sentence states the array's contents accurately. And "~630" is not a fabricated figure — it is the codebase's consistent shorthand for per-district evaluated positions, used correctly at district-detail.ts:739, snapshot-types.ts:9 and scripts/build-snapshot.mts:241. Only the verb "are present" is wrong for the field being annotated; a charitable reading ("all ~630 reach this filter — nothing is sampled away, unlike the national board's two-per-(district,tier)") is coherent and is plainly the paragraph's thrust.

So this is a real factual misstatement in a load-bearing docstring — not a style opinion, and the project's number-vs-artefact discipline makes comment drift meaningful — but it ships no wrong number, misleads no judge, and breaks no behaviour. That is "low".
